events.label: AMD AI Day Day 1 (San Francisco) — MI400 roadmap + Microsoft Azure Helios win as anchor
events.note: AMD AI Day opens July 21 in San Francisco (Day 2 is July 22). AMD enters Day 1 with a significant tailwind: Microsoft Azure announced deployment of AMD Helios Rackscale Solution (AMD MI-series + EPYC + Pensando DPUs) for large-scale AI inference in Azure data centers, with delivery H2 2026. This is the first hyperscaler win that directly addresses the Kimi K3 AI-capex-disruption thesis from July 17. Day 1 must deliver: (1) MI400 competitive roadmap vs. NVDA Blackwell; (2) explicit response to Kimi K3 inference-economics challenge; (3) additional hyperscaler or large-enterprise customer wins beyond Microsoft. AMD closed at ~$511 (+3.83%) on July 20 on the Microsoft news — Day 1 information trades against that elevated expectation. Hold above $510 = constructive; fall below $500 = disappointment trade. Kimi K3 open-weight release on July 27 means AMD has a five-day window after AI Day to set the narrative before the second AI efficiency wave.

events.label: TSLA Q2 2026 earnings (AH) + GOOGL Q2 earnings (AH) + Intel Q2 + AMD AI Day Day 2 — week's defining binary
events.note: The week's most consequential risk event — four major catalysts on the same day. TSLA Q2 AH: 480K deliveries (best Q2 ever) are known; gross margin >15% (from ~14% Q1) is the base case, >18-20% is the re-rate gate above $410. GOOGL Q2 AH: Cloud backlog $462B (40%+ QoQ); 43/53 analysts Strong Buy; must address Gemini 3.5 Pro delay, Kimi K3 competitive threat, and EU $4.67B antitrust fine (July 20 disclosure) in addition to AI Overviews monetization and capex trajectory. AMD Microsoft Azure Helios deal (July 20) reduces the Kimi K3 narrative pressure on GOOGL Cloud entering the print. Intel Q2: enterprise semiconductor demand bellwether — guidance on budget cycles (one-quarter vs. multi-year) is the enterprise-software read (NOW, CRM, ACN). AMD AI Day Day 2 closes the MI400 roadmap. A GOOGL Cloud beat + TSLA margin beat = formal STEP ASIDE → HOLD upgrade conditions in play (if SPX closes above 7,480 Wednesday). A single miss on any dimension extends STEP ASIDE through FOMC.

events.label: Kimi K3 full open-weight model weights public release — second AI narrative wave; largest open-source AI model ever by parameter count
events.note: Moonshot AI scheduled to release the full Kimi K3 model weights (2.8 trillion parameters) publicly on July 27 — five days after AMD AI Day (July 22-23) and one week after GOOGL/TSLA earnings. AMD's Microsoft Azure Helios win (July 20) partially neutralizes the AI-capex-disruption premise heading into this event. If July 22 earnings confirm AI demand thesis (GOOGL Cloud beat, TSLA margin beat), July 27 open-weight release will be less impactful. If July 22 disappoints on any major dimension, the open-weight release could re-activate the second DeepSeek trade and extend the semiconductor bear market beyond AMD AI Day. The five-day window (July 22-26) is the semiconductor sector's best opportunity to recover narrative ground before the second efficiency wave arrives. Do not add NVDA into July 27 — Kimi K3 open weights are a known risk catalyst.

events.label: FOMC meeting (Jul 28-29) — July hold probability 86.7%; September hike probability 48.7% (first close below 50%)
events.note: As of July 20 night: July hold probability 86.7%; September hike probability 48.7% (compressed from 69% on July 17 to below 50% on July 20 — the first sub-50% close since the Hormuz crisis began). Brent $87.72 (July 20 settlement) still embeds material August CPI oil-shock risk, but the rate-compression trend is the most constructive signal since the conflict escalated. The September language in the FOMC statement is the market-moving variable: dovish September language = immediate rate relief and potential STEP ASIDE → HOLD upgrade; hawkish September 50bps confirmation = rate-shock regime extends through Q3. Key watch: August CPI (est. Aug 13) is the primary FOMC input; WTI above $80 for 10+ consecutive sessions through the July 14-20 window is fully loaded into August energy components regardless of daily settlement moves.

events.label: META Q2 2026 earnings — AI cloud business quantification; MSFT + AMZN also; peak Q2 earnings week
events.note: META Q2 earnings July 29 is the first event where management must quantify the AI cloud business (Bloomberg July 1: Meta building AI cloud to sell excess compute). MSFT Azure must validate the AMD Helios deployment narrative with actual Azure AI revenue growth data. AMZN AWS is the third major hyperscaler read on AI demand thesis. META's ad-driven model is most insulated from Kimi K3 demand disruption. GOOGL reports July 22 (earlier). Peak Q2 earnings risk window.

events.label: July CPI release (est. Aug 13) — WTI above $80 for 10+ sessions + Brent $87.72; most consequential macro print of 2026
events.note: July CPI is the first release to fully capture the WTI formal $82.21 settlement (July 20) and persistent Brent $87-90 range amid the ongoing Iran Hormuz blockade. The FOMC is pricing ~48.7% probability of a September hike as of July 20 (first close below 50%). Bull scenario (August CPI <3.2% YoY with oil-shock not embedding in core): September hike probability collapses below 30%, BUY conditions open formally. Bear scenario (August CPI >3.5% YoY with WTI/Brent oil-shock passing through to services/transportation): September 50bps probability jumps, BEARISH regime extends through Q4. June CPI 0.0% MoM demonstrated prior shocks did not embed; the July shock magnitude (Brent $87-90, WTI $82+, 10+ consecutive sessions above formal triggers) is structurally larger and more sustained than any prior 2026 oil event.

events.label: NVDA Q2 FY27 earnings (est.) — $91B revenue guide; AI capex cycle clearing event; addresses Moonshot AI + TSMC wafer hike
events.note: NVDA's Q2 FY27 earnings is the fundamental clearing event for the AI capex thesis. $91B revenue guidance represents sequential acceleration. AMD's Microsoft Azure Helios win (July 20) provides positive read-through for hyperscaler AI hardware demand. Risk factors: (1) TSMC 5-10% wafer price hike across 74% of wafer revenue = 2-4pp gross margin headwind management must quantify; (2) Moonshot AI Kimi K3 (July 17) is a frontier-class open-weight model at 70% pricing discount that challenges hyperscaler GPU cluster inference demand — Kimi K3 open weights release July 27 will have occurred two months prior; (3) September hike probability at 48.7% applies a reduced-but-real discount-rate headwind to NVDA's 37x forward multiple. NVDA held the $195 hard stop through the July 14-20 selloff — do not add until post-Q2 FY27 print with wafer hike impact clarified and Kimi K3 demand impact quantified.

events.label: SPCX first earnings as a public company (approx.) — Starlink ARR + Starship cadence
events.note: First earnings print since June 12 IPO. SPCX touched an intraday all-time low of $132.75 on July 15 (below $135 IPO price) — down 30%+ from June 16 ATH of $225.64. 27 of 31 analysts still carry Buy ratings; the sell-side downgrade cycle has barely begun. December 2026 lock-up expiry adds supply overhang. Re-entry gate: first earnings print (Starlink ARR growth, Starship launch cadence, cash burn) is the fundamental clearing event. Net losses are structural ($4.9B in 2025, $4.28B in Q1 2026). Better entry $115-120 for risk-tolerant 12-month investors.

events.label: SPCX 180-day IPO lock-up expiry (approx.) — insider/early-investor float unlock
events.note: ~180 days after the June 12 debut, early investors and insiders can sell, materially expanding the ~4% public float. Lock-up expiries are a known supply overhang for hot IPOs. The $20B bond offering (June 22) already changed the capital structure risk profile — the lock-up expiry adds equity supply overhang.

events.label: OpenAI IPO — target window shifts to H1 2027 after 2026 delay
events.note: OpenAI delayed its anticipated 2026 IPO to H1 2027 (announced June 26, 2026). SoftBank sold off -13% on the delay. Microsoft and NVIDIA hold strategic stakes. The delay removes a near-term AI sentiment catalyst and adds uncertainty to AI infrastructure spending trajectories.
